::: {.why}
Four weeks of modelling run off one feature matrix, so an alignment error made today is an error in every result until day 238.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Assemble a feature matrix with an explicit as-of date per row and no forward-filled values crossing an availability boundary.
- Have a test that fails if any feature value in a row postdates that row's as-of date.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build qlib/ml/dataset.py: rows keyed by security and as-of date, features pulled through the store's as-of interface, labels computed forward from the as-of date with the lag convention applied. Handle missingness explicitly with an indicator rather than imputing, because for most of these features missing is informative.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Write the guard test: for a sample of rows, check every feature value against the store's own availability timestamp and assert none postdates the row. Then rerun the day 155 poisoned-future test through the model pipeline rather than through the engine, since the model path is new and untested.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
qlib/ml/dataset.py assembles the feature matrix through the store's as-of interface with a test that no feature value postdates its row. The poisoned-future test now covers the model path as well as the engine.
:::
